panels.title: Broker acknowledgement attempts
panels.description: ACK success follows completed action or SQL commit. ACK transport failure can follow committed work and never triggers rejection. Reject failures are separate from action failures.

panels.title: Outbox phases p95
panels.description: Claim includes transaction commit. Publish covers one claimed room prefix, including deadline checks. Complete includes SQL transaction commit. These overlapping or concurrent percentiles cannot be added.

panels.title: Outbox batch outcomes
panels.description: Each attempt records once: empty means no claimed rows, work means claimed work without dependency failure, failed includes claim, Redis publication or SQL completion failure. Work can leave rows unattempted at the deadline.

panels.title: Claimed rows retained for retry
panels.description: Rows left pending by each attempt: failed publication and unattempted room tail, unattempted deadline work, or Redis-confirmed rows whose SQL completion failed. Counts can repeat across retries; this is not the backlog gauge or a unique-event count.

panels.title: Outbox row age at publication start
panels.description: Time from persisted SQL created_at to each Redis publication attempt. The database default uses transaction start, so age includes work before commit, claim waiting and earlier events in the room. Missing and future timestamps are excluded and counted by messenger_outbox_publication_age_invalid_total. These percentiles overlap other stages and cannot be added.

panels.title: Maximum current quorum-queue commit latency
panels.description: At each scrape, the RabbitMQ collector takes the maximum reported commit latency across quorum queues on each node. A queue value can remain unchanged while idle. This is not a time-window maximum or p99, and does not isolate disk fsync. Compare with publisher confirmation and SQL commit timing.
